doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Playing bass in the kitchen and editing the episodes
summary: Discussion of episode four with the bass and chicken, her husband's editing of hours of footage down to under fifteen minutes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Yeah, I have one suggestion with episode four — you could have another subtitle, like how to use the electric bass in the kitchen. I wondered if that was —

Yeah my dad was angry at that, he said that was really stupid. I said well that’s the point. We’re not trying to take ourselves too seriously. You know I thought well let’s just grab the bass and we’ll pound the chicken. My husband looked at me and he said, “No you’re not going to do that.” I said, “Watch me,” and I just did it. He says, “I don’t know if we’re going to use it.” And I said, “Yeah, you will.” And he did. Because I give him sort of the choice of how to edit because it takes us, because it’s two people doing the job of ten here. You know we’re trying to do multiple camera shoots but it’s only the two of us. And so we’re trying to — oh what was I going to say, you know, figure out how to — so it takes so long, he has to do so much editing. And he has good taste so I leave all the editing choices up to him and edit down what would be like three or four hours into under fifteen minutes if possible.
